deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding pages of §§1-4). X is a topological space and F is a family of subsets of X satisfying axioms a)-f). Roughly:
- a)-c): Boolean-algebra and closure/interior stability, i.e. 'constructible-type' sets.
- d): F is generated by its locally closed members.
- e): descending-chain condition. A chain A_1 ⊃ A_2 ⊃ ..., with each term relatively closed and rare in the previous one, is stationary at the empty set. This is a finite-dimensionality axiom.
- f): every member of F has finitely many connected components, and these lie in F.

§4 introduces a subfamily F_r ⊂ F of locally closed sets, called 'F-regular' sets. These are an abstract stand-in for smooth (sub)manifolds. Condition (S) requires that every locally closed Y ∈ F has a largest relatively open subset Y_reg lying in F_r. Moreover Y_reg must be dense, so that Y_sing = Y − Y_reg is rare in Y.

This page.

Definition. A finite partition (cellular decomposition) P of X into members of F is F-regular if two things hold. First, its leaves are in F_r (the parenthetical says so). Second, for every closed P-saturated Y, the singular locus Y_sing is again P-saturated. This is an abstract analogue of a stratification whose strata are smooth and in which 'singular locus of a union of strata is a union of strata'.

Proposition. Assume a), b), c) on F and (S) on F_r. Then for every finite subfamily L ⊂ F there exist:
- an F-regular partition of X compatible with L (each Y ∈ L is a union of leaves);
- a coarsest such partition.
If F also satisfies f), the same holds for F-regular partitions with connected leaves.

Proof sketch.
- One may assume L is stable under the relevant operations (frontier, closure, complement).
- Put X' = ⋃_{Y∈L} (Ẏ ∪ Y_sing), with Ẏ the frontier, and U = X − X'.
- Each Y ∩ U is then open and closed in U, and regular.
- Iterate, as for the U_i of the previous page, adding the (U_i)_sing to L at each stage. With f), first pass to the connected components of U.
- Termination comes from the chain condition e).

Corollaries.
1. F is the filtered union of the F_P, with P running over F-regular partitions (resp. with connected leaves).
2. F-regular partitions admit finite sups (in the coarsening order).
3. There is a canonical F-regular partition of X: the coarsest one, i.e. the case L = {X}.

The purpose is to build, inside an axiomatic 'tame topology', canonical smooth-type stratifications refining any finite family of tame sets. This is the abstract version of the canonical stratification by iterated singular loci.
errors: Showing that Y∩U ⊂ F_r needs F_r to be stable under passage to open (or relatively open) F-subsets. Y∩U is open in Y and misses Y_sing, so it lies in Y_reg; but being in F_r requires this heredity, which is not stated.

Coarsest-partition claim: one must show that X' (frontiers and singular loci of L-sets) is saturated for every F-regular partition compatible with L. The definition only controls Y_sing for closed saturated Y. Saturation of frontiers or closures of saturated sets (a frontier-type condition) is not part of the stated definition, so the minimality argument has a gap unless it is built in.

Termination: the Y_sing are rare in Y but not necessarily in X, and are not closed in X. To apply e) one has to work with closures and relatively closed chains. This is only sketched ('on continue comme plus haut').
There is an inconsistency between 'f)' (connected leaves, as on the previous page) and 'd)' in Cor. 1 and the line 'dans le cas où F satisfait d)'. Connected-component arguments need f).

ideas.what: Abstract 'regularity' subclass F_r of a tame family F, with axiom (S): a largest regular open dense part Y_reg of every locally closed tame Y, with rare singular locus.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic smooth locus / regular points in o-minimal or tame geometry (e.g. the definable C^p-smooth locus is open dense)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Concrete case: Whitney, Łojasiewicz (semialgebraic/analytic); o-minimal: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (1980s-90s)
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic call for 'topologie modérée' and stratified structures in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6

ideas.what: F-regular partitions: finite partitions into regular tame leaves such that singular loci of closed saturated sets are saturated; existence compatible with any finite family, existence of a coarsest one, and of finite sups.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical (coarsest) stratification by iterated singular loci; minimal stratifications compatible with finitely many definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney (1965); Teissier (canonical Whitney stratification, 1982); o-minimal versions: van den Dries 1998, Loi, Nguyen–Trivedi–Trotman
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only alludes to dévissage of tame spaces into strata

ideas.what: Representing F as a filtered union of the finite Boolean algebras F_P attached to regular partitions.
ideas.modern_name: Definable sets as a directed union over stratifications (constructible sets via stratifications)
ideas.where_published: Analogous ideas for constructible sets in EGA IV §9 and SGA 4/5 (constructible sheaves via stratifications)

missed.claim: An axiomatic stratification theorem. It is relative to an abstract regularity class F_r, with no differentiable structure assumed, and yields a canonical coarsest regular stratification and sups of stratifications, all from a few axioms (Boolean, chain condition, finite components, and (S)). The literature proves such statements separately for each regularity notion (C^p, Whitney, Verdier) in o-minimal structures. It does not state a single abstract existence-of-coarsest result parametrized by a 'regularity' predicate.
missed.quote: il existe une partition F-régulière de X, et une plus grossière telle partition ... Cor 3) Partition F-régulière canonique de X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Such an abstraction could unify canonical-stratification results: minimal Whitney, Verdier, or Lipschitz stratifications in o-minimal geometry. It anticipates (1974) the axiomatic tame-topology framework later developed as o-minimality.

deep.surprise_reason: The theorem itself (canonical stratification by iterated singular loci) is classical in concrete settings. The novelty lies in the 1974 axiomatic formulation, with an abstract regularity class inside a tame family, predating o-minimality. This is of historical interest but only sketched, and it has gaps.
transcription_corrections: 'si L de F est une partie fermée' should likely read 'si L ⊂ F est une partie finie' (finite subfamily).
'Si F satisfait d), alors il existe une partition F-régulière de X : feuilles connexes' – the image appears to read 'satisfait f)'.
'il existe une partition F-régulière ... feuilles connexes' – the image reads 'une partition F-régulière de X à feuilles connexes, et une plus grossière telle'.
'Donc P est une feuilletée de F_P' is more plausibly 'Donc F est réunion filtrante des F_P, où P parcourt les partitions à feuilles F-régulières'.
'Ẏ' presumably denotes the frontier of Y.
'Sup bis' is likely 'Sup finis' (finite sups exist).
